schema_name: Prometheus Cross-Unix Evidence-First Security Audit Knowledge
purpose: A cross-platform, non-executable library of proposed audit checks and epistemic guardrails, not a certified benchmark or instructions to modify a host.

platform_vocabulary.linux: Linux general; distribution and version verification required
platform_vocabulary.linux:systemd: Linux only when systemd is the relevant service manager

status_vocabulary.NOT_EVALUATED: No check executed or evidence collected
status_vocabulary.PASS: Observed state meets selected documented policy with sufficient evidence
status_vocabulary.FAIL: Observed state demonstrably contradicts selected documented policy
status_vocabulary.REVIEW: Evidence exists but needs interpretation, risk acceptance or investigation
status_vocabulary.UNKNOWN: Missing tools, permissions, incomplete observations, unverified assumptions or unavailable policy
status_vocabulary.NOT_APPLICABLE: Feature/workload confirmed absent or out of scope

foundational_rules: Never label a test PASS merely because a file or service exists.
Never invent thresholds, secure defaults or universal permissions.
Keep observation separate from expected policy and decision.
Commands in inspection.strategy are illustrative, not shell scripts; resolve aliases/version support before use.
A read-only audit must not install, enable, configure, rotate, vacuum, download or delete anything.
Never assume Linux, systemd, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and NetBSD have interchangeable utilities or semantics.
Absent tool means UNKNOWN unless irrelevant feature is confirmed NOT_APPLICABLE.
Risk labels are preliminary triage suggestions, not policy-backed severity ratings.
Do not inspect or print actual credential contents; metadata first.
Versioned authoritative sources and tested checks are required before production compliance claims.

inspection.strategy: read metadata of actual password database only; use stat syntax appropriate to platform
